findings: anchors=[extraction, live-page]: recipetineats fetched clean and confirms the transcription verbatim (same 9 ingredients, servings 4-6, same 40-covered + 50-uncovered bake). Battery fails ruled as follows. (1) ingredient-coverage INVENTED 'Fresh Sage' beside DROPPED 'fresh sage leaves' is the head-noun rule reporting a pure naming pairing, same food, present in the buy list and used in the add-to-pot step - defensible, NOTE only. (2) scale-ratio Salt 3.0x vs recipe 3.5x: exact scale is 2 1/3 tbsp, spec buys 2 tbsp, a 14% under-round on a line the source itself marks 'plus more to taste' - defensible rounding, NOTE (owner=mapper if a repair is ever wanted). (3) prose-numbers 'intro_html says 2g fat' is a battery parse artifact: the prose actually says '46.2 grams of fat' and the regex split the decimal; the real residue is prose 46.2 vs stat 46, a rounding remainder, NOTE owner=writer to prefer the stat's own integer. Substitution judged on merits: source's 1/2 cinnamon stick became 1 3/4 tsp ground cinnamon (documented deliberately in the spec's own notes, method says ground to match the buy string, conversion within normal stick-to-ground range at 3.5x) - defensible, NOTE. Method survives whole: brown, drain fat, add cinnamon/sage/lemon zest/garlic/milk, bake covered 40 then uncovered 50 (1.5 hr), rest ~5 min, serve unstrained with curds - the source's wash step dropped is a food-safety improvement, not a dish change. Lemons correctly zest-only at 7 (2 x 3.5); milk 8 cups vs exact 7.875 quantization-explained; 3 whole chickens is sane whole-unit scaling of one 3-3.5 lb bird at 3.5x. Title, credit and URL match. Same dish throughout.
